Subject: Re: CTLHealth DPA - initial redline and questions on subprocessors / transfers

Marissa —

Thanks for the redline. A few quick notes from counsel (attached: counsel_annotated_dpa.pdf):

- Transfers: CTLHealth will want to see either executed SCCs or an EU-US Addendum for EU-origin data. They have some internal procurement constraints that prefer the Addendum route; we'll confirm which exact variant.
- Subprocessors: request to preserve a 30-day prior notice window + right to object in a specific carve-out (health-data processing).
- Security obligations: counsel wants an explicit reference to encryption-in-transit and at-rest, plus a short list of controls (ISO 27001 / SOC 2 reference acceptable).

Two technical Qs for Redwood:
1) How do you handle cross-region KV cache replication? Is there an option to prevent EU->US replication for CTLHealth-specific workloads?
2) Can you provide a copy of the subprocessor flow we should present to CTLHealth procurement (we saw Subprocessor_Matrix.xlsx but need a plain-language description for non-technical reviewers).

We can do a call tomorrow 09:30 ET to walk counsel through the redline if that works. Otherwise we will send our annotated DPA back with proposed wording.

Attachments: [Attachment: counsel_annotated_dpa.pdf (PDF)]

Best,
Harper Davis

Subject: Re: CTLHealth DPA - initial redline and questions on subprocessors / transfers

Thanks, Marissa / Harper. Quick counsel notes and proposed language (summary below) — I can provide tracked changes if you want.

Summary of recommended changes:
- Transfers: offer EU-US Addendum + option for SCCs if procurement insists. Add sentence: "Where applicable, the parties shall enter into the EU-US Data Transfer Addendum (or other lawful transfer mechanism) for transfers of personal data from the EEA to the United States."
- Subprocessors: accept 30-day notice, propose a 10-business-day objection period limited to documented processing risks (our standard). Sample clause: "Controller may object within 10 business days on reasonable grounds relating to data protection; failure to object constitutes acceptance."
- Security: include references to encryption-in-transit and at-rest, provide SOC 2 Type II attestation on request, and commit to encryption keys managed by Redwood (BYOK optional under Private deployment).

Action items for the group:
- Rishi: can you prepare a one-page plain-language subprocessor summary for CTLHealth procurement (include hosting regions, third-party analytics, monitoring providers).
- Marissa: confirm whether CTLHealth requires BYOK or if KMS integration note suffices for now.
- Harper: please confirm whether CTLHealth's procurement will accept the Addendum or insist on SCCs.

Attachments: [Attachment: redlines_summary.pdf (PDF)]

Neha Kapoor
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
